atoms.text: The Jurassic Coast is a World Heritage Site in Dorset, England. The coastline has around 185 million years of history and provides an insight into the UK’s prehistoric heritage. Almost all the rocks on the Jurassic Coast are sedimentary rocks. During the Jurassic times the Jurassic Coast was submerged in water meaning it is now one of the most renowned locations to find fossils.

atoms.text: On Dorset’s Jurassic Coast, there is a famous stone arch called Durdle Door. It is formed of limestone. Limestone is a soft, permeable rock which means that it is easily effected by water erosion. It formed as a result of the sea gradually pushing through the limestone around 10,000 years ago.
